cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Choose the Precedent
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which rule, custom, or prior decision will govern what happens now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The usual arrangement. Who gets the head seat: Grandma or the birthday child? We have traditions for both.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly how we always do it. Fine. Which tradition decides who gets served first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Serve them together. Except there's only one birthday pudding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose before I bring it in: elders first or birthdays first? I can divide the pudding once somebody's had the wish.

mechanism: A copies a sun-avoidance chair turn as seating precedence and asks B to choose which tradition governs the unresolved shared resource.
confusable: D178 demands chosen precedent; D179 treats ambiguous interpretation as loyalty.
comparison: Permit scope and supper versus elder/birthday customs and a single pudding.
seedUse: Keep B two-chair and joint-service solutions until the one pudding forces a real choice.
